display.title: Episode 227: Lag BaOmer and the Calculator, the Rashbi's Day of Joy (Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Lag BaOmer show: a calculator and a pair of tzitzis explain why Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's yahrzeit is a day of joy, plus a victory march, two young Shema guests and contest winners.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Lag BaOmer itself. Uncle Yossi explains that 'Lag' is 33 in Hebrew letters and that the day is the yahrzeit of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who asked that it be celebrated as the day of his joy. Why celebrate a passing? Following the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to learn from everything, he has listeners take out a calculator and add up the letters of the word tzitzis with its knots and strings to reach 613, pressing 'total' only at the end. So too, every mitzvah we do is written in a heavenly book and keeps adding up all our lives; when a tzaddik's soul returns to Hashem, the total of all his Torah and mitzvos is revealed, a bright and joyous day. In the merit of Rabbi Shimon we can hope for victory, 'Didan Notzach', celebrated with a new Hakochainik victory march. After a sponsor message, two small children say the Shema in Studio 604, and the first winners of the Sefer Torah contest are announced; each wins a small Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah adds to your lifelong total, so keep adding more Torah and mitzvos every day; and celebrate Lag BaOmer with joy.

date.note: Confirmed by the audio: 'Here we are celebrating Lag BaOmer' (18 Iyar).

advisories.note: Explains a tzaddik's passing and the soul's reward in Gan Eden.

privacy.note: Two young Shema guests and two contest winners named in full.

sources_cited.note: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai calls the day of his passing a day of joy (hilula).
'You shall see it and remember all the mitzvos': tzitzis equals 613.
'All your deeds are written in a book.'
'Kedai hu Rabbi Shimon lismoch alav bish'as had'chak': we may rely on Rabbi Shimon's merit in a time of need.

segments.title: The calculator lesson: why Lag BaOmer is a day of joy
segments.summary: Adding up tzitzis to 613 shows how a lifetime of mitzvos is totaled on a tzaddik's yahrzeit, making the Rashbi's day one of joy.

segments.title: The merit of Rabbi Shimon: Didan Notzach
segments.summary: In difficult times we may rely on Rabbi Shimon's merit, and expect victory.

segments.title: Sefer Torah contest: the first grand winners
